candidates.name: Direct dense query (bi-encoder ANN) — baseline
candidates.what: Encode the query (speech vector) once and run faiss ANN against utterance/word keys; the current mock. No generation, no fusion.
candidates.evidence: FIXED-PIPELINE (mock = this). The zero-lever reference every other candidate is measured against.

candidates.name: HyDE — hypothetical-document embedding
candidates.what: Frozen omni generates a hypothetical answer to the query, embed that, retrieve with it instead of the raw query. Deterministic single generation.
candidates.evidence: FIXED-PIPELINE compatible (one greedy generation + one embed). Gao et al. HyDE; 2025 variants report large precision/recall lifts. Speech-native 'hypothetical spoken answer' embedding is unexplored (gap).

candidates.name: HyPE — hypothetical prompt embeddings (per-document)
candidates.what: Offline, generate the questions each KB value could answer and index THOSE; query matches question-space at run time. Optimizes per-document not per-query.
candidates.evidence: FIXED-PIPELINE (fully offline; zero run-time generation, unlike HyDE). Search-snippet: reports up to +42pt precision / +45pt recall vs plain retrieval (not opened).

candidates.name: Adaptive-HyDE (threshold-lowering, never-empty)
candidates.what: HyDE plus a rule that auto-lowers the similarity threshold when the top hit is weak, to guarantee non-empty, partially-relevant context.
candidates.evidence: FIXED-PIPELINE (rule-based threshold, no learning). arXiv 2507.16754 (opened): 7 pipelines/63 variants, HyDE+full-answer best, beats zero-shot on 4 OSS LLMs by LLM-judge; no hard numbers in abstract.

candidates.name: LLM query rewrite / expansion (single-pass)
candidates.what: Frozen omni rewrites or term-expands the query before encoding; one deterministic pass.
candidates.evidence: FIXED-PIPELINE. Baseline lever. RL-trained rewriters (below) are the adaptive escalation.

candidates.name: Multi-query / multi-embedding fan-out (AMER, multi-view)
candidates.what: Generate several query views/embeddings and union their retrieved sets before ranking.
candidates.evidence: FIXED-PIPELINE if generation is deterministic. Search-snippet: AMER autoregressively emits multiple query embeddings, beats single-embedding (not opened).

candidates.name: Self-query — LLM-constructed metadata filters
candidates.what: Frozen omni parses the query into (semantic vector + structured filter) and applies the filter over KB metadata — directly usable to gate our grain tag (knowledge/memory/exemplar), speaker, language, emotion facets.
candidates.evidence: FIXED-PIPELINE (LangChain/LlamaIndex self-query, well-established). Strong fit to our grain-tagged values; no speech-facet self-query paper exists (gap/opportunity).

candidates.name: Cross-modal asymmetric encode — Speech-to-Retrieval (S2R)
candidates.what: Map the spoken query directly to an embedding via an audio query-encoder trained against a separate document-encoder; retrieve without ASR, avoiding transcription-error propagation.
candidates.evidence: FIXED-PIPELINE (encoders frozen at inference). Google S2R, live in production, multilingual (opened marktechpost 2025-10): beats ASR-then-retrieve on Simple Voice Questions, approaches perfect-transcript upper bound; WER shown NOT to predict retrieval quality. Position vs SpeechRAG/VoxRAG: same ASR-free thesis, but S2R is a jointly-trained asymmetric dual-encoder rather than cascade.

candidates.name: Query decomposition into sub-queries (DecomposeRAG)
candidates.what: Split a complex query into simpler sub-queries, retrieve each, merge. Can run at fixed breadth.
candidates.evidence: FIXED-PIPELINE at fixed depth; ADAPTIVE if depth/priority is query-conditioned. Search-snippet: DecomposeRAG SOTA on multi-hop QA (not opened).

candidates.name: Latent-space query reasoning (AdaQR / LaSER)
candidates.what: Produce reasoning in embedding space rather than text, yielding a retrieval-tuned query vector at low latency.
candidates.evidence: OUT-OF-MOCK (some variants trained). Search-snippet only (not opened). Listed for completeness.

candidates.name: RL-trained query rewriter (TongSearch-QR / ConvSearch-R1 / RAR2-DPO)
candidates.what: Train a small model with RL/DPO (thinking + performance reward) to rewrite queries for retrieval.
candidates.evidence: OUT-OF-MOCK (weight updates). The training-free analogue = reward-guided best-of-N over rewrite candidates using the frozen omni's own signal (W1 machinery). Search-snippet (not opened).

candidates.name: Iterative feedback query expansion (ThinkQE / DIVER-QExpand)
candidates.what: Refine the expansion across rounds using retrieval feedback; DIVER keeps only original+final round to cap token growth.
candidates.evidence: INHERENTLY ADAPTIVE (feedback loop → step-3). Search-snippet (not opened).

candidates.name: Hybrid sparse+dense fusion (RRF / convex combination)
candidates.what: Fuse a lexical list (BM25 over transcripts, or phonetic/discrete-speech-token n-grams) with the dense list via RRF (k≈60) or convex α-blend.
candidates.evidence: FIXED-PIPELINE. Search-snippet evidence: hybrid +7.4% NDCG over either alone (WANDS); convex α=0.5 Recall@5 0.726 > RRF 0.695 (not opened). Speech twist: what plays the 'sparse' role over speech keys (discrete units/phonetic) is an open design choice.

candidates.name: Late-interaction multi-vector retrieval (ColBERT/PLAID; Col-* for speech)
candidates.what: Keep token/frame-level key vectors and score by MaxSim; word-level speech keys are the natural multi-vector unit.
candidates.evidence: FIXED-PIPELINE but NOT native to faiss/llama.cpp — needs a PLAID-style engine. PLAID: 45x CPU / 7x GPU latency cut vs ColBERTv2 (snippet). ColPali proves the pattern for vision (patches); no speech-frame Col-* analogue exists (gap).

candidates.name: Frozen cross-encoder reranker (BGE-reranker class)
candidates.what: Second-pass (query,candidate) joint scoring to reorder the ANN shortlist. For speech, operates on transcripts or omni-scored pairs.
candidates.evidence: FIXED-PIPELINE. Snippet: cross-encoders deliver ~95% of LLM-rerank accuracy at 3x lower latency. No cross-encoder scoring (speech-query, speech-key) directly (gap).

candidates.name: LLM listwise reranker, zero-shot (RankGPT-style on the frozen omni)
candidates.what: Prompt the frozen Qwen3-Omni to read the candidate list and emit a reordered permutation — reuses the model we already host.
candidates.evidence: FIXED-PIPELINE, training-free, uses the resident llama-server. Snippet: listwise > pointwise/pairwise; +5-8% accuracy but +4-6s latency vs cross-encoder. Cheapest high-value rerank lever for us.

candidates.name: Setwise / groupwise reranking (Setwise, GroupRank)
candidates.what: Score groups of candidates per LLM call to cut the number of comparisons vs full listwise.
candidates.evidence: FIXED-PIPELINE. Efficiency-oriented listwise. GroupRank arXiv 2511.11653 (snippet, not opened).

candidates.name: Distilled open listwise rerankers (RankZephyr / RankVicuna / Rank-without-GPT)
candidates.what: Drop-in frozen listwise rerankers distilled from GPT, no local training.
candidates.evidence: FIXED-PIPELINE (frozen checkpoints). Snippet via RankLLM toolkit (not opened).

candidates.name: RL-trained reasoning reranker (REARANK / Rank-R1 / Rank1 / ERank)
candidates.what: Train an LLM reranker with GRPO to reason-then-rank; REARANK on Qwen2.5-7B.
candidates.evidence: OUT-OF-MOCK (weight updates). REARANK arXiv 2505.20046 (opened): GRPO, only 179 MSMARCO queries →12k, +4.49 nDCG@10 BEIR, +2.7 BRIGHT (beats GPT-4), +5.91 TREC-DL. This is exactly the object a training-free reward-guided reranker would target WITHOUT weights.

candidates.name: Fixed-depth iterative / multi-hop retrieval (IRCoT-style, k rounds)
candidates.what: Interleave retrieval with reasoning for a fixed k rounds; deterministic budget.
candidates.evidence: FIXED-PIPELINE at fixed k (mock-compatible). Becomes adaptive only when k is query-conditioned.

candidates.name: Adaptive stopping for iterative retrieval — training-free (TASR)
candidates.what: Stop retrieving at the first round where the answer repeats AND the calibrated logit-margin > 0.25; variable depth per query.
candidates.evidence: INHERENTLY ADAPTIVE (variable depth) but TRAINING-FREE (only a 1-D isotonic calibrator fit once on 100 Q, frozen). arXiv 2606.13814 (opened): F1 57.40 @3.13 calls, +3.42 vs fixed-k=3, 94.8% of fixed-k=5 F1 at 62.6% cost; transferred to a 550B model. Cleanest bridge from mock to step-3 because it needs no policy training — llama.cpp exposes the logprobs it needs. Position vs TARG/NEST gating line: TASR gates the LOOP via self-confidence, not per-token retrieval.

candidates.name: Adaptive iterative w/ learned control (FLARE / Self-RAG / SeaKR / Stop-RAG)
candidates.what: Trigger/stop retrieval on generation confidence, reflection tokens, or a value function.
candidates.evidence: INHERENTLY ADAPTIVE (step-3). FLARE=token-prob threshold, Self-RAG=reflection tokens (trained), Stop-RAG=value-based (arXiv 2510.14337, snippet). Reward-guided training-free versions are the W1-style opportunity.

candidates.name: Query routing by complexity (Adaptive-RAG router; tier-based)
candidates.what: Classify query complexity and route: no-retrieval / single-shot / multi-hop.
candidates.evidence: ADAPTIVE (needs a classifier) but a RULE-based router (e.g. on self-confidence/length) is mock-compatible. Adaptive-RAG T5-Large 3-class router matches always-expensive at lower cost; RAGRouter-Bench 7,727 queries (snippets, not opened).

candidates.name: Distraction-aware retrieval (LDAR)
candidates.what: RL policy learns to drop retrieved passages that are relevant-but-misleading, beyond similarity scoring.
candidates.evidence: OUT-OF-MOCK (policy-gradient trained). arXiv 2509.21865 (opened): beats standard retrieval and long-context with fewer tokens; distractor-filtering is the target a training-free reward-guided selector could approximate.

candidates.name: Online-optimized retrieval (deployment-time embedding gradients)
candidates.what: Nudge item embeddings at deployment from binary success/failure feedback (success→toward query, failure→away).
candidates.evidence: OUT-OF-MOCK and NOT weight-frozen — it mutates the index embeddings via SGD (not RL). arXiv 2509.20415 (opened): +3-9% Recall@10/NDCG@10 on UltraTool/ToolRet/FiQA/MultiHopRAG, negligible latency. Included as the anti-pattern boundary: this VIOLATES our frozen-KB constraint; a training-free lever must NOT edit the index.

candidates.name: Relevance-edge reordering (lost-in-the-middle mitigation)
candidates.what: Place the highest-scoring retrieved items at the start and end of the prompt, weakest in the middle.
candidates.evidence: FIXED-PIPELINE, training-free, essentially free. Lost-in-the-middle U-curve persists in 2025 models (Chroma context-rot: GPT-4.1/Claude4/Gemini2.5/Qwen3 all non-uniform). Untested on OMNI models with interleaved audio tokens (gap).

candidates.name: Attention-basin-aligned reordering
candidates.what: Measure the model's position-attention profile and map the most relevant item to the highest-attention slot.
candidates.evidence: FIXED-PIPELINE, training-free reorder. arXiv 2508.05128 (opened): 'attention basin' — non-uniform position attention; training-free repositioning improves long-context QA/retrieval/summarization. Feasibility risk: needs attention read-out, not exposed by default in llama.cpp.

candidates.name: Extractive prompt compression (LLMLingua-2 / LongLLMLingua)
candidates.what: Drop low-information tokens from retrieved context before injection using a small frozen token classifier.
candidates.evidence: FIXED-PIPELINE (LLMLingua-2 = frozen BERT-level classifier). Snippet: LongLLMLingua +17.1% at 4x compression; LLMLingua-2 3-6x faster, OOD-robust. Text-only — compressing retrieved AUDIO/embedding values for an omni model is unexplored (gap).

candidates.name: Abstractive summarization before injection (RECOMP-Abst / summ-retrieval)
candidates.what: Summarize retrieved passages into a short synopsis before prepending.
candidates.evidence: FIXED-PIPELINE. Load-bearing: arXiv 2501.01880 (opened) finds SUMMARIZATION-based retrieval ≈ long-context while CHUNK-based lags — a direct steer toward summarize-then-inject over raw chunks.

candidates.name: Attention-guided context pruning (AttentionRAG)
candidates.what: Prune retrieved context by attention relevance to the query focus.
candidates.evidence: FIXED-PIPELINE-ish. arXiv 2503.10720 (snippet, not opened). Same llama.cpp attention-access feasibility risk as attention-basin reorder.

candidates.name: Soft / embedding context compression (xRAG)
candidates.what: Map retrieved context to a few dense latent vectors via an MLP, injected as soft tokens.
candidates.evidence: OUT-OF-MOCK for a FROZEN model (needs a trained projector/adapter into the model's input space). Snippet. Interesting because our KB already stores embeddings — but injecting them into a frozen omni requires an alignment adapter.

candidates.name: Performance-driven RL context compression (CORE)
candidates.what: RL-trained compressor keeps only chunks that raise downstream answer performance.
candidates.evidence: OUT-OF-MOCK (RL-trained). arXiv 2508.19282 (opened): beats no-compression and LLMLingua at higher compression. Target for a training-free reward-guided keep/drop selector.

candidates.name: Flat prompt injection — baseline delivery
candidates.what: Concatenate retrieved values into the prompt in similarity order.
candidates.evidence: FIXED-PIPELINE (mock delivery baseline). Reference for reorder/compress/structured levers.

candidates.name: Structured / tool-form delivery (retrieval as a tool-call)
candidates.what: Expose retrieval as a function schema (search(query, grain, speaker)); the frozen omni emits a tool call and consumes structured results.
candidates.evidence: FIXED-PIPELINE if a single forced tool call; ADAPTIVE if the model chooses when/which to call. llama.cpp supports Qwen3 tool-calling. Snippet: agentic tool-routing shows 15-20% retrieval-quality lift over static configs (the adaptive version).

candidates.name: Logical / Boolean structured retrieval (LogicalRAG)
candidates.what: Frozen omni emits a Lucene-style Boolean query (AND/OR/NOT, phrase, field); inverted index gates candidates, BM25 ranks — separates 'what can be retrieved' from 'what ranks'.
candidates.evidence: FIXED-PIPELINE, TRAINING-FREE. arXiv 2605.27123 (opened): matches agentic hybrid on KILT (0.717 vs 0.716 judge-acc), 41x faster build, 2.3x throughput, 3.1x lower latency, 35% less hallucination when evidence absent; stronger models reach parity. Note: gains scale with model capability — a 30B omni is a plausible sweet spot.

candidates.name: GraphRAG / structured subgraph retrieval + delivery
candidates.what: Model KB entities/edges as a graph; interpret query, select a subgraph, assemble community summaries + linked values.
candidates.evidence: FIXED-PIPELINE possible (precomputed graph) but multi-hop. Snippet: GraphRAG-Bench 2025 — GraphRAG > vanilla on complex reasoning/summarization; gap narrows for simple fact lookup. Heavy to build over speech keys; speaker/turn graph is a speech-native angle (gap).

candidates.name: Grain-typed delivery with role markers
candidates.what: Deliver retrieved values explicitly labeled by grain (knowledge/memory/exemplar) with role framing, so the frozen model treats a fact vs a recalled instance vs a demonstration differently.
candidates.evidence: FIXED-PIPELINE. Design lever native to our KB schema (not a single paper); pairs with self-query filtering. No prior work delivers grain-typed speech-KB values to an omni — clean whitespace.

candidates.name: Long-context stuffing (no retrieval) — comparison arm
candidates.what: Dump all/most candidate context into the window, no selection.
candidates.evidence: FIXED-PIPELINE baseline arm. arXiv 2501.01880 (opened): long-context wins on Wikipedia factual QA; RAG wins on dialogue/general. For OMNI, audio tokens are context-expensive — the tradeoff likely shifts hard toward RAG (unbenchmarked, gap).

candidates.name: Isotonic-calibrated self-confidence primitive
candidates.what: Fit a 1-D isotonic map (once, ~100 Q) from the frozen model's logit-margin to correctness probability; a reusable signal for stop/route/rerank gating.
candidates.evidence: FIXED-PIPELINE, training-free-compatible (calibrator ≠ policy). From TASR (opened). llama.cpp exposes logprobs; this is the cheapest reusable confidence primitive for later reward-guided levers.

candidates.name: RRF / convex fusion primitive
candidates.what: Rank-fusion operator to merge any two ranked lists (e.g. speech-dense + phonetic-sparse, or two query views).
candidates.evidence: FIXED-PIPELINE. Trivial to implement over faiss outputs; enables the hybrid and multi-query candidates.

candidates.name: Asymmetric dual-encoder primitive (query-enc ≠ key-enc)
candidates.what: Allow the speech query-encoder and the KB key-encoder to differ, aligned by contrastive/KALE-style post-hoc alignment.
candidates.evidence: Enabling primitive for S2R-style cross-modal encode. Our KB currently likely uses one embedder for keys; supporting an asymmetric query path is a build cost but unlocks ASR-free speech-query retrieval.

claims.claim: Google Speech-to-Retrieval (S2R) maps a spoken query directly to an embedding via an audio query-encoder jointly trained against a separate document-encoder, retrieves without ASR, is live in production multilingually, beats ASR-then-retrieve on Simple Voice Questions and approaches the perfect-transcript upper bound; they show reducing WER does not reliably improve retrieval.
claims.source: Google Speech-to-Retrieval (S2R), MarkTechPost coverage, 2025-10-12 (opened full article)
claims.relevance: Directly validates cross-modal asymmetric encode for our speech-vector-keyed KB and positions us against SpeechRAG/VoxRAG (cascade-avoidance) with a bi-encoder that is jointly trained, not cascaded.

claims.claim: TASR stops iterative retrieval at the first round where the model repeats its previous answer AND the calibrated logit-margin exceeds 0.25; it is training-free (only a 1-D isotonic calibrator fit once on 100 questions, frozen), scores F1 57.40 at 3.13 calls (+3.42 vs fixed-k=3; 94.8% of fixed-k=5 F1 at 62.6% cost), and transfers to a 550B model with no regressions.
claims.source: TASR: Training-Free Adaptive Stopping for Iterative Retrieval, arXiv 2606.13814 (opened HTML)
claims.relevance: Cleanest training-free bridge from the fixed mock to step-3 adaptivity: variable retrieval depth using only the frozen model's logprobs, which llama.cpp exposes. Advances beyond the TARG/NEST per-token gating line by gating the retrieval LOOP via self-confidence.

claims.claim: LogicalRAG has the LLM emit Lucene-style Boolean queries (AND/OR/NOT, phrase, field) over an inverted index (BM25 ranks); training-free, it matches agentic hybrid dense-sparse on KILT-scale Wikipedia (0.717 vs 0.716 judge-accuracy) with 41x faster build, 2.3x throughput, 3.1x lower latency, and 35% lower hallucination when evidence is absent, with gains growing as model capability rises.
claims.source: Rethinking Agentic RAG: LLM-Driven Logical Retrieval Beyond Embeddings, arXiv 2605.27123 (opened HTML)
claims.relevance: A training-free structured/tool-form delivery where the FROZEN omni constructs the query; capability-scaling means a 30B omni is a plausible sweet spot. Alternative to pure dense retrieval that keeps the KB frozen.

claims.claim: Attention Basin: LLMs allocate non-uniform attention across positions; a training-free reordering that moves important items to attention-favored positions improves long-context QA, retrieval and summarization without any weight update.
claims.source: Attention Basin: Why Contextual Position Matters in LLMs, arXiv 2508.05128 (opened PDF)
claims.relevance: Grounds a near-free delivery lever (context reordering). Caveat: requires an attention read-out that is not exposed by default in llama.cpp; the relevance-edge reorder variant needs only scores and is trivially implementable.

claims.claim: Lost-in-the-middle persists in 2025 frontier models: Chroma's context-rot report over 18 models (incl. GPT-4.1, Claude 4, Gemini 2.5, Qwen3) finds context is not used uniformly and reliability degrades with input length; placing top-scoring documents at the start/end edges mitigates it.
claims.source: Lost-in-the-middle 2025 syntheses incl. arXiv 2510.10276 and Chroma context-rot (search snippets, not opened)
claims.relevance: Justifies relevance-edge reordering as a delivery lever; flags that this is entirely untested on OMNI models whose contexts interleave audio tokens.

claims.claim: In a filtered evaluation, long-context generally beats RAG on Wikipedia-based factual QA while RAG wins on dialogue/general queries; crucially, summarization-based retrieval performs comparably to long-context whereas chunk-based retrieval lags, and context relevance is the overlooked variable.
claims.source: Long Context vs. RAG for LLMs: An Evaluation and Revisits, arXiv 2501.01880 (opened abstract)
claims.relevance: Steers delivery toward summarize-then-inject over raw chunk injection, and frames the long-context-vs-RAG arm; for an omni model audio tokens are context-expensive so the tradeoff likely tilts to RAG (unbenchmarked).

claims.claim: REARANK is an RL-trained (GRPO, Qwen2.5-7B) reasoning reranker using only 179 MSMARCO queries augmented to 12k, gaining +4.49 nDCG@10 on BEIR, +2.7 on BRIGHT (surpassing GPT-4), and +5.91 on TREC-DL.
claims.source: REARANK: Reasoning Re-ranking Agent via RL, arXiv 2505.20046 (opened HTML)
claims.relevance: Defines the trained-reranker object; the training-free counterpart is reward-guided best-of-N reranking with the frozen omni (W1 machinery) — same target, no weights.

claims.claim: CORE compresses RAG context via RL driven by downstream answer performance and beats both no-compression and LLMLingua at higher compression ratios; LLMLingua-2 (a frozen BERT-level token classifier) is training-free and 3-6x faster with OOD robustness, and LongLLMLingua reports +17.1% at 4x compression.
claims.source: Less Is More / CORE, arXiv 2508.19282 (opened PDF); LLMLingua family (Microsoft, search snippets, not opened)
claims.relevance: Separates the training-free compression lever (LLMLingua-2, mock-compatible) from the RL-trained one (CORE, step-3 target). All are text-only — audio/embedding-value compression for omni is a gap.

claims.claim: Learning Distraction-Aware Retrieval (LDAR) uses policy-gradient RL to drop retrieved passages that are relevant-but-misleading (distractors), beating standard retrieval and long-context with fewer tokens.
claims.source: Beyond RAG vs. Long-Context: Learning Distraction-Aware Retrieval, arXiv 2509.21865 (opened PDF)
claims.relevance: Shows similarity-top-k is not the right selection objective; a training-free reward-guided selector approximating distractor-filtering is a step-3 lever over our frozen KB.

claims.claim: Online-Optimized RAG updates item/tool embeddings at deployment via importance-weighted SGD from binary success/failure feedback (success moves embedding toward query, failure away), gaining +3-9% Recall@10/NDCG@10 across UltraTool/ToolRet/FiQA/MultiHopRAG with negligible latency.
claims.source: Online-Optimized RAG for Tool Use and Function Calling, arXiv 2509.20415 (opened HTML)
claims.relevance: Boundary/anti-pattern: it MUTATES the index (not frozen) and is gradient-based, so it violates our frozen-KB + training-free constraint — a useful contrast for what our levers must NOT do.

claims.claim: Adaptive-HyDE (developer support) sweeps 7 pipelines / 63 variants, finds HyDE-plus-full-answer-context best, and adds a rule to auto-lower the similarity threshold to guarantee non-empty partially-relevant context; it beats zero-shot across 4 OSS LLMs by LLM-as-judge (no hard numbers in abstract).
claims.source: Never Come Up Empty: Adaptive HyDE Retrieval, arXiv 2507.16754 (opened HTML)
claims.relevance: HyDE remains a live, mock-compatible query-construction lever; the threshold-lowering rule is a cheap never-empty fix. Speech-native 'hypothetical spoken answer' HyDE is unexplored.

claims.claim: Hybrid BM25+dense fusion beats either alone (e.g. +7.4% NDCG on WANDS); convex combination at alpha=0.5 reached Recall@5 0.726 vs RRF(k=60) 0.695; RRF needs no score calibration while convex blending uses raw scores.
claims.source: Hybrid search 2025-26 syntheses incl. ceur-ws Vol-4173 and mbrenndoerfer/denser.ai (search snippets, not opened)
claims.relevance: Supports a hybrid-fusion candidate; open question for speech keys is what fills the 'sparse' role (phonetic/discrete-unit n-grams over utterance/word keys).

claims.claim: Late-interaction multi-vector retrieval (ColBERT) scores by summing per-query-token MaxSim over passage tokens; PLAID cuts latency up to 45x on CPU / 7x on GPU vs ColBERTv2 via centroid interaction; ColPali extends the pattern to document-image patches (1024 patch embeddings/page, MaxSim) removing OCR.
claims.source: PLAID arXiv 2205.09707; ColPali arXiv 2407.01449 (search snippets, not opened)
claims.relevance: Late interaction is the natural fit for word-level speech keys, but is not native to faiss/llama.cpp (needs a PLAID-style engine); no speech-frame Col-* analogue exists — a clean gap.

claims.claim: Adaptive iterative RAG decides retrieval timing/stopping via prompting-, confidence-, or training-based paradigms (IRCoT interleaves CoT+retrieval; FLARE triggers on low token probability; Self-RAG uses trained reflection tokens; Adaptive-RAG routes with a T5 complexity classifier; Stop-RAG uses a value function).
claims.source: Iterative/adaptive RAG syntheses incl. Stop-RAG arXiv 2510.14337, SeaKR 2406.19215 (search snippets, not opened)
claims.relevance: Maps the adaptive-depth landscape; most require training or trained tokens, so the training-free, reward-guided-on-frozen-omni variant (à la TASR + best-of-N) is the whitespace.

claims.claim: Self-query retrieval uses an LLM to decompose a natural-language query into a semantic vector plus structured metadata filters, then executes a filtered vector search (hybrid of semantic + structured constraints).
claims.source: LangChain/LlamaIndex self-query & auto-retrieval docs, 2025 (search snippets, not opened)
claims.relevance: Direct mechanism to gate our grain-tagged values (knowledge/memory/exemplar) plus speaker/language/emotion facets from omni embeddings; a mock-compatible query-construction lever with no speech-specific prior art.

claims.claim: Agentic RAG turns retrieval into a learned policy where the agent chooses retriever, top-k, reranker depth and chunk size per query, with early systems reporting 15-20% retrieval-quality lift over static configurations; retrieval is exposed as a tool-call (search(query)) via structured function schemas.
claims.source: Agentic RAG 2025-26 syntheses (labelyourdata, futureagi; search snippets, not opened)
claims.relevance: Frames structured/tool-form delivery and the adaptive per-query configuration selection that a training-free reward-guided controller (step-3) would target while keeping the model frozen.

claims.claim: HyPE precomputes, per document, the hypothetical questions each document answers and indexes those (question-space keys), optimizing per-document (fully offline) rather than per-query like HyDE.
claims.source: HyPE 2025 (search snippet via HyDE emergentmind/mlplus coverage, not opened)
claims.relevance: An alternative key-organization angle: index the value in question-space; offline so zero run-time generation cost, unlike HyDE.

gaps:
EXPLICIT GAPS / WHITESPACE for our frozen-omni + faiss speech-KB program (Dimension 3):

1. SPEECH-NATIVE RERANKING is missing. Every reranker surveyed (cross-encoders, RankGPT/RankZephyr, REARANK, GroupRank) scores text or transcripts. No cross-encoder or LLM reranker scores (speech-query, speech-key) pairs directly in speech-vector space. S2R is a bi-encoder, not a reranker. Opportunity: use the frozen omni itself as a listwise reranker over speech candidates (training-free, reuses our llama-server).

2. SPEECH/EMBEDDING-VALUE COMPRESSION is missing. LLMLingua-2/LongLLMLingua/RECOMP/AttentionRAG/CORE all compress TEXT. Compressing retrieved audio segments or embedding-valued KB entries before injecting to an omni model is unexplored; soft-compression (xRAG) would need an alignment adapter into a frozen omni's input space.

3. LATE-INTERACTION OVER SPEECH FRAMES is absent. ColBERT/PLAID (text) and ColPali/ColQwen (image patches) prove multi-vector MaxSim, but there is no frame/word-level Col-* for speech keys — the natural representation for our word-level keys. Also NOT native to faiss/llama.cpp (needs a PLAID-style engine): a build-cost + feasibility risk to flag.

4. HyDE-FOR-SPEECH unexplored: a 'hypothetical spoken answer' embedding (omni generates, we embed the audio/omni-state) as a query-construction lever has no prior work; only text HyDE/HyPE exist.

5. POSITION / ATTENTION-BASIN effects UNMEASURED ON OMNI. All lost-in-the-middle and attention-basin work is text-token; behavior when the context interleaves audio tokens is unknown. Feasibility: attention-basin/AttentionRAG reordering need attention read-out not exposed by default in llama.cpp (only the relevance-edge reorder, needing scores alone, is trivially implementable now).

6. SELF-QUERY OVER OMNI FACETS is a clean opportunity, not a paper: no work has the frozen omni construct metadata filters over grain tags (knowledge/memory/exemplar) + speaker/language/emotion facets derived from omni embeddings. Pairs with grain-typed delivery.

7. TRAINING-FREE ADAPTIVE RETRIEVAL is thin. The adaptive-depth/selection landscape (FLARE, Self-RAG, Adaptive-RAG, LDAR, CORE, online-opt) is almost entirely TRAINED (classifiers, reflection tokens, policy gradients, or index-mutating SGD). TASR is the lone training-free adaptive-stop (isotonic calibrator only) and it gates the LOOP, not SELECTION/rerank/query-construction. WHITESPACE = a training-free, reward-guided controller that uses ONLY the frozen omni's own signals (logit-margin, answer stability, best-of-N over retrieval configs — the W1 best-of-N machinery) to pick query construction / top-k / rerank order / stop, while the KB stays frozen. Note the hard constraint boundary: Online-Optimized RAG mutates the index, which our frozen-KB rule forbids.

8. LONG-CONTEXT-vs-RAG FOR OMNI is unbenchmarked. Audio tokens are context-expensive, so the text-domain finding (long-context wins Wikipedia QA; summarization-retrieval ≈ long-context; chunk-retrieval lags) may not transfer; the tradeoff likely tilts harder to RAG for omni but no one has measured it.

9. STRUCTURED-vs-FLAT DELIVERY on speech KB untested. LogicalRAG (Boolean/inverted-index) and GraphRAG (subgraph) are text/entity graphs; a speaker/turn/session graph or Boolean-over-transcript-fields delivery for a speech KB, and whether a 30B omni is capable enough for LogicalRAG's capability-scaling regime, are open.

10. HYBRID SPARSE ROLE FOR SPEECH undefined: RRF/convex fusion assumes a lexical (BM25) list; what plays 'sparse' over speech keys (phonetic n-grams, discrete-unit strings, transcript BM25) and how to fuse it with the dense speech-vector list is an unresolved design choice, not covered by any surveyed paper.
